dossier.public_summary: The 1.1-day dip lines up with the star’s 1.1-day spot rotation and appears off-centre and too long for the small M-dwarf, with huge phase-curve swings and wildly varying depths. Centroid imaging says the dip is on the target, so it is not a blended neighbour – it is the star’s own variability (spot occultations) folded at the rotation period.

reasons.why: Observed duration 1.49 h is much longer than central duration 0.8299 h expected for TIC radius 0.28 Rsun (star_density_penalty 113.2, fit_log_density_ratio -2.486, fit_b 0.7367). Signal is consistent with stellar activity occultation of spots, not a planet transit.

rotation 1.099 d (sector 17 amplitude 26972 ppm, false_alarm 7.867229510825339e-127; sector 58 1.095 d amplitude 19503 ppm; sector 85 1.101 d amplitude 18628 ppm) equals signal period 1.0967 d (signal_at_rotation_multiple 1). Phase_curve amplitude 4396 ppm ratio_to_depth 1.149 chi2 117 dof 9 shows large out-of-transit modulation at this period, as expected for spots, not a planet.

56 transits not consistent (chi2 105.69449286688592 dof 55, share_of_top_3 0.589); outliers depth_ppm 22452 sigma 6.5 and 17751 sigma 4.8 show spot-like variability. Depth varies by sector (1820 ppm sector 17 vs 4241 ppm sector 58) but centroid.verdict on_target with suspects ruled out >4 sigma, so signal is on target but astrophysical from star, not a background blend.
